test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 22 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In the context of Budget, the salaries pensions, defence services the comes under ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Revenue Expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Expenditure** refers to the expenditure incurred by the government for the day-to-day operations and maintenance of services and other recurring expenses. This includes **salaries, pensions, and defense services**.
 
• It does not result in the creation of assets or reduction of liabilities. For example, paying salaries and pensions is a recurring expense and does not add to the capital assets of the government.
 
• As per the classification of government finances, **Revenue Expenditure** is a major component of the Revenue Budget, which deals with the regular functioning of the government and its services.
 
• Expenditures such as **interest payments** on loans, subsidies, and grants to state governments and other institutions are also included under Revenue Expenditure.
 
• **Salaries, pensions, and defense services** fall under this category because they are recurring operational costs essential for the functioning of the government. Hence, the correct option is Revenue Expenditure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Revenue Receipts:**

 
 
• These are the incomes received by the government that do not create liabilities or reduce assets. Examples include **tax revenue** (like income tax, GST) and **non-tax revenue** (like interest receipts, dividends).
 
• Unlike Revenue Expenditure, Revenue Receipts do not involve any outgoing expenses.
 
 
 
• **Capital Expenditure:**
 
 
• This refers to government spending on the creation of assets like infrastructure, buildings, and machinery or the reduction of liabilities.
 
• Examples include **construction of highways, bridges, and schools**.
 
• It is non-recurring in nature and contributes to the long-term development of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Capital Receipts:**
 
 
• These are receipts that lead to an increase in liabilities or a reduction in assets. Examples include **borrowings, disinvestments, and recovery of loans**.
 
• They are non-recurring in nature and are usually used to finance Capital Expenditure or repay past borrowings.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Revenue Expenditure:**
 
 
• It ensures the functioning of essential services like defense, healthcare, education, and public administration.
 
• It supports welfare schemes and subsidies that directly benefit the citizens.
 
• Revenue Expenditure is critical for maintaining law and order and ensuring national security through defense spending.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Budget Classification in India:**

 
 
• The Union Budget is divided into two main components: **Revenue Budget** and **Capital Budget**.
 
• The Revenue Budget includes Revenue Receipts and Revenue Expenditure, while the Capital Budget includes Capital Receipts and Capital Expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Revenue Expenditure:** Payment of **salaries, pensions, subsidies, interest on loans, and defense expenses.**
 
• **Examples of Capital Expenditure:** Construction of **infrastructure, acquisition of machinery, and capital investments.**
 
• **Fiscal Policy and Revenue Expenditure:** Revenue Expenditure plays a significant role in influencing fiscal policy outcomes, such as stimulating demand in the economy or controlling inflation.
